findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hot holding units in the back of the cook line and part of the one on the cook line to not be holding temperature within the appropriate temperature range. PIC mention that the unit in question sometimes malfunction with temperature holding. They will work on getting an upgrade to a more functional unit. Ensure that these units is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) The jug of milk in the chest cooler that holds the ice cream condiments was observed to not be date marked properly. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the milk was opened the previous day. PIC instructed a staff member to properly date mark the milk jug. The jug was dated immediately. Ensure that all food items not used be properly date marked if it is going to be stored for more that 24 hour after opening. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff barehandling ready to eat food items during food prep. Discussed with PIC and an education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are aware to don gloves after handwashing before prepping ready to eat food at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed quat sanitizer in all of the sani buckets to have a concentration between 0 and 100 ppm. findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Observed sauteet mushrooms to have a temperature of 110 degrees. The mushrooms had been placed in the hot holding approximately 3 hours prior. The mushrooms were immediately heated to a temperature of 165 degrees F or higher. Additionally, more water was added to the steam table the mushrooms were on and the temperature was turned up.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Observed live cockroaches on glue traps during the inspection near the dish machine. Additionally, there were dead cockroaches under the ice cream machine. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate cockroaches, using proper pest control processes as needed. It is recommended to punch holes in walls to determine the source of the cockroaches. When that is completed, the holes must be cleaned and filled. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Employee was observed cleaning with sanitizer rags and then immediately placed gloves on to return to food prep without washing hands first. Employee was stopped and hand washing discussed. Employee discarded gloves, washed hands and then continued.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Employee did not wash hands after eating/drinking/smoking. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Quaternary ammonium solution in sanitizer buckets both on the make line and near the drive thru tested at 0 ppm quaternary ammonium. Buckets are prepared from the wall mounted dispenser at the three compartment sink, which was dispensing at 200 ppm. Buckets were remade.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Adult and juvenile, live roaches are observed in the facility most notably near the ice machine corner in the kitchen, behind the custard machine, and under the dish machine. This has been an ongoing issue and the pest control operator is making weekly visits to resolve. No roaches were observed on the make line. Follow up in 10 days regarding this issue.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The top of the coving to the left of the custard topping station is heavily soiled with debris accumulation. Clean this area and maintain clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: There are numerous juvenile and adult roaches observed throughout the facility--under/behind the ice machine, under ice cream machine, under dish machine, under back hand sink. There are glue traps on the front counter with dead adult roaches observed. Bacon's Pest Control was last here on 9/26/19 per invoice. The facility purchased gel from Bacon's and also uses a spray (not on food contact surfaces) and glue boards. Consult pest control immediately as there is rampant activity today.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) . The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Grout in tile in front of ice machine/to left of custard machine is deep and no longer easily cleanable. Roaches observed in this area. Also observed roaches go under black coving on wall to right of ice machine where there are gaps in the grout. Tile needs re-grouted to help eliminate pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) Floors, Walls and Ceilings were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed fish in the fish station cooler that was probed to be 49-54F. This cooler was not plugged in when it was set up and therefore was not operating. Cooler was plugged in at the time of the inspection. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth draped over the side of the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen and not enough sanitizer solution in the bucket to keep all the cloths submerged in solution in between use. There was also a wet wiping cloth sitting on the table next to the prep sink. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed the tongs in the prep cooler next to the grill to be stored in contact with the foods (cooked chicken tong handles were stored touching the chicken, raw ground beef tong handles stored touching the ground beef). The same cook handles both of these tongs; therefore it is important to keep the handles extended up and out of the foods to protect from cross contamination.  3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed old date marking labels on several of the in use lids in the custard station. For instance, containers with custard toppings such as cookie dough had labels that said cucumbers on it. Remove old date labels before being run through the dish machine. 4-603.12  (C) If necessary for effective cleaning, UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives. Reference 4-603.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) Observed the sanitizer bucket on the make line to test at 0 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. Quat from the wall mounted dispenser was dispensing at 200-400 ppm. Bucket was re-made and must be changed as often as necessary to provide the proper concentration. 2) Observed the trays that are being used for food assembly to not be washed, rinsed and sanitized as per employee. These must be washed, rinsed and sanitized or changed out with clean at least every 4 hours in use. 
4-501.114  (P)  Maintain concentration of quaternary ammonium solution at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11 (P) Except as specified in ¶ (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours. P

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed scoop handle in the pecans in the back to be stored in contact with the pecans. Make sure scoop handle extends up and out of the food as this is not a food that requires further cooking.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: Observed the faucet on the left at the three compartment sink to drip when off even with handles as tight as possible. Repair plumbing to eliminate drip.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C)  Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.
